lines: Before anyone joins a Popkin, they find it. Here is the front door.
A visitor opens the landing page and reads: Your people, popped up in seconds. One button, Start a Popkin. Free. Takes about a minute.
With it, a preview of a Popkin: Lakeside Weekend, fourteen here, wraps up Sunday.
Scan. Join. You're in. Three steps: Pop one up. Share the QR code. You're together.
Then four ideas, for every group that forms around a table.
A Small group that keeps going. A Hackathon, for one weekend. A Team, for one season. A Family trip, for ten days.
Better than a group chat. Five rows say why: joining, photos, plans, video, and the end.
Muted forever, or a proper send-off and recap.
Free. Like, actually free. No ads, no premium tier.
In the navigation, How it works and Ideas jump to their sections, and focus moves to the heading.
On a phone, the navigation keeps Start a Popkin. Sign in is in the footer.
Start a Popkin opens sign-up. Sign in opens sign-in.
And a person who is already signed in skips the page: they get My Popkins.
Then the welcome screen. The same promise, and three ways on: Start a Popkin, Join with a code, and: Already have an account? Sign in.

lines.text: On a phone, the landing page is one column.
From ten twenty-four pixels, the hero sits beside its preview, and the four ideas run across.
And from seven sixty-eight, the welcome screen is split.

lines: What no screen shows: the page loads nothing from anywhere but Popkin, and its links work from the keyboard.
Still to come: the Join with a code screen, and Safety, Privacy and Help.
That is journey ten. Popkin is a free platform for pop-up communities.
